entities.summary: Manuel Álvarez Bravo was a Mexican artistic photographer and one of the most important figures in 20th century Latin American photography. He was born and raised in Mexico City. While he took art classes at the Academia Nacional de Bellas Artes, his photography is self-taught. His career spanned from the late 1920s to the 1990s with its artistic peak between the 1920s and 1950s. His hallmark as a photographer was to capture images of the ordinary but in ironic or Surrealistic ways. His early work was based on European influences, but he was soon influenced by the Mexican muralism movement and the general cultural and political push at the time to redefine Mexican identity.

His work contributed to the development of a unique visual language that reflected Mexico's cultural and political landscape.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Manuel Álvarez Bravo's photography played a significant role in shaping Latin American identity during the mid-20th century, influencing generations of photographers and artists. His work, which often combined everyday life with surrealist elements, contributed to the development of Mexican modernism.
